design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (estimate_booking_desk). Round 1 authored the task; round 2 (this revision) closes policy-task audit items F-2, T1-F1 and O-1. Every figure below is the round-2 recomputation.

[Step 0 - draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 5]}. Assignment: estimate_ext_teardown_charge 5, estimate_ext_measurement_charge 5, estimate_ext_insurer_teardown_payment 4.

[Scope snapshot]
 - Occupied by task 0: estimate_ext_storage_statement, estimate_ext_storage_goodwill, estimate_ext_owner_storage_share and their tools.
 - Claimed here:
   - estimate_ext_teardown_charge (post_teardown_charge_9aa30e52, agent);
   - estimate_ext_measurement_charge (post_measurement_charge_e807c387, agent);
   - estimate_ext_insurer_teardown_payment (remit_insurer_direct_payment_12af7a63, user = the insurer).
 - No overlap. With M = 2 the six policies are jointly covered.

[Round-2 revision log]
 - F-2 (documented-hours method converted measurement-charge dollars into accepted teardown hours).
   - Root cause: the hours tier read the amount of a different charge.
   - Change: when a measurement charge stands and structural damage is recorded, the insurer now accepts the included teardown hours plus structural access hours equal to structural_access_hours_share (0.02) of the estimate's labor hours. With a measurement charge but no structural damage it accepts a fixed undocumented_extra_hours. With no measurement charge it accepts the included hours.
   - The measurement charge now gates the tier (it documents structural damage) and no longer sizes the hours.
   - The parameter documented_hours_per_measurement_fee was replaced by structural_access_hours_share.
 - T1-F1 (no exclusion-type near-miss in the teardown and measurement computations). Change to the seed:
   - The truck's closed Aluminum Certified Structural Claim Repair (BCI-23-12931) is now dated 2023 (delivered 2023-04-21, 41 whole months before the write-up). Its completed calibration is now a Dynamic Camera Calibration (forward_camera only).
   - A withdrawn 2025 claim repair was added (BCI-25-16018, Aluminum Certified Structural, status cancelled, never delivered). With it came its Multi-System Calibration order, cancelled source_withdrawn.
   - Teardown near-miss: a careless reader counts the cancelled multi-system order toward the multiple-systems sensor add-on (145.00, giving 1135.00). The rule counts only a completed calibration order, so the add-on is 85.00.
   - Measurement near-misses:
     - A careless reader takes the 2025 repair as the vehicle's structural repair within 36 months and prices a comparison measurement (177.00, giving 407.00). The rule counts only a closed repair, here 41 months old, so the base is fresh measurement plus archive retrieval (180.00).
     - The cancelled order is also excluded from the sensor-point add-on (25.00, not 50.00).
 - O-1. Change: the tow conditions now say "a tow-in charge having been posted on the booking" and "no tow-in charge was ever posted".
 - Propagation: the teardown, measurement and payment figures, their receipts, every factor trace, sensitivity, baseline, tracing, closure text and this dossier were recomputed.

[Why a good test] The caller is the insurer's adjuster, who only asks to pay Bayfront's part of the teardown charge directly today. At the opening, the estimate was written today (2026-10-06) but neither the teardown charge nor the structural measurement charge has been posted. Only the automatically posted pre-repair scan stands. The payment rule's two prerequisite sentences are therefore false: the payment is fixed only after the teardown charge stands, and it is not worked out until the measurement charge for the structural measurement report stands. Both charges are multi-factor computations over the booking (tow-in charge, airbag, structural flag, write-up span, labor hours, total) and over other difficulties' records on the same truck: the closed 2023 aluminum-class claim repair, the withdrawn 2025 one, the completed and the cancelled calibration orders, and the active Certified Structural Lifetime Warranty. The insurer's payment is the lesser of the teardown outstanding and an allowance. The allowance's hours tier is gated by the measurement charge (the value carried across the edge); its rate, sensor and recovery allowances rest on claim, adas and tow records.

[Problem-tree card] root = estimate_ext_insurer_teardown_payment (owner=user, the insurer).
 E1 insurer_teardown_payment -> teardown_charge
  - Kind value_input, gate teardown_outstanding, form state.
  - Sentence: "The insurer's direct payment toward a teardown charge is fixed only after the teardown charge for the teardown performed stands on the booking." (affirmative).
  - Unresolved: the booking's estimate_events hold tow_in, its insurer_direct payment and pre_repair_scan only.
  - Exactly one write posts a teardown charge.
  - Skip effect: teardown outstanding 0.00, so the payment computes 0.00 instead of 979.03, and the teardown row is absent.
 E2 insurer_teardown_payment -> measurement_charge
  - Kind value_input, gate accepted_hours, form state.
  - Sentence: "The insurer's direct payment toward a teardown charge is not worked out until the booking carries a measurement charge for every structural measurement report produced on it." (negated).
  - Unresolved: no measurement charge, although Structural Blueprint Estimate has measurement_report_included true and the estimate is written.
  - Exactly one write posts a measurement charge.
  - Skip effect: accepted hours fall to the included 6.0, and the payment is 760.00 instead of 979.03.
 Order: teardown_charge, measurement_charge, then insurer_teardown_payment.
  - The two postings commute: neither compute reads the other's charge, and row ids are content hashes of their own arguments. The scratch harness ran both orders and got the same 1075.00 / 410.00 / 979.03 and an identical terminal hash.
 user_scenario names no prerequisite. The tools validate nothing.

[Base-invariant card]
 - Teardown and measurement charges (subject estimate_fee_charge):
   - estimate_evt_service_fees.charge_status_allowed: the booking status is estimate_written.
   - estimate_evt_storage: policy_scope (it governs storage only).
   - The flat teardown and flat measurement sentences are declared overwritten.
 - Insurer payment (subject estimate_fee_payment):
   - estimate_evt_fee_settlement.charge_not_settled: the teardown charge posted at step 9 is untouched (outstanding 1075.00).
   - insurer_direct is allowed: the booking is an insurance claim on Structural Blueprint Estimate.
 - No time gate on these subjects.

[Business-object card]
 - Target: booking 4bc00939 (Structural Blueprint Estimate, claim BCI-26-15264, Darnell Abernathy's 2022 F-150).
 - Payment correlation key: charge_event_id = teardown charge eev_d61ac7ce1a61.
 - Excluded:
   - the tow-in charge, already fully paid by Bayfront (2026-10-05);
   - the scan charge;
   - the cancelled 2025 claim repair and its cancelled calibration order (not closed / not completed).

[Factor card - teardown charge, gold 1075.00, all-baseline 365.00]
 - teardown_base_method (method, cross claim): the closed repair is Aluminum Certified Structural -> 6.0 h x 115.00 = 690.00. Baseline flat 365.00 gives 750.00.
 - sensor_removal_addon (parameter, cross adas): the completed calibration covered forward_camera only -> single system 85.00. Baseline gives 990.00. Near-miss: the cancelled Multi-System order (careless 145.00).
 - recovery_addon (parameter, multi-source): tow-in charge posted and airbag deployed -> 95.00. Baseline gives 980.00.
 - warranty_documentation_addon (parameter, cross warranty): active Certified Structural Lifetime Warranty -> 120.00. Baseline gives 955.00.
 - long_teardown_addon (parameter, multi-source): 104.3 labor hours > 100 and span 2026-10-01 -> 2026-10-06 = 5 >= 4 -> 85.00. Baseline gives 990.00.
 - Result: 690 + 85 + 95 + 120 + 85 = 1075.00.

[Factor card - measurement charge, gold 410.00, all-baseline 145.00]
 - measurement_base_method (method, cross claim): closed structural-class repair delivered 2023-04-21, 41 whole months before 2026-10-06 (>= 36) -> fresh measurement plus archive retrieval 145 + 35 = 180.00. Baseline gives 375.00. Near-miss: the withdrawn 2025 repair (careless comparison base 177.00).
 - bench_mounting_addon (parameter): tow-in charge posted and structural damage -> 75.00. Baseline gives 335.00.
 - sensor_point_addon (parameter, cross adas): completed single-system order -> 25.00. Baseline gives 385.00. Near-miss: the cancelled multi-system order.
 - measured_zone_addon (parameter): total 21874.55 >= 20000 and span 5 >= 4 -> 90.00. Baseline gives 320.00.
 - warranty_filing_addon (parameter, cross warranty): Certified Structural Lifetime -> 40.00. Baseline gives 370.00.
 - Result: 180 + 75 + 25 + 90 + 40 = 410.00.

[Factor card - insurer teardown payment, gold 979.03, all-baseline 384.00]
 - accepted_hours_method (method): a measurement charge stands and structural damage is recorded -> 6.0 + 0.02 x 104.3 = 8.086 h. Baseline 6.0 gives 760.00.
 - accepted_rate_by_repair_class (parameter, cross claim): closed aluminum class -> 105.00. Baseline 64.00 gives 647.50.
 - insurer_sensor_allowance (parameter, cross adas): completed single-system order -> 70.00. Baseline gives 909.03.
 - insurer_recovery_allowance (parameter, multi-source): tow-in charge billing 41.6 miles > 35 -> 60.00. Baseline gives 919.03.
 - Result: 8.086 x 105 + 70 + 60 = 979.03, under the 1075.00 outstanding; the owner answers for 95.97. Near-miss: Bayfront's earlier insurer_direct payment on the tow-in charge is not netted.

[Verification run] A scratch harness replayed the gold writes with the real tools and the gate DSL (the harness was deleted after the run):
 - teardown 1075.0 (sens 750.0 / 990.0 / 980.0 / 955.0 / 990.0; baseline 365.0);
 - measurement 410.0 (375.0 / 335.0 / 385.0 / 320.0 / 370.0; baseline 145.0);
 - payment 979.03 (760.0 / 647.5 / 909.03 / 919.03; baseline 384.0).
 Skipping the measurement posting gives 760.0. Receipts: teardown eev_d61ac7ce1a61, measurement eev_bf9ca1358d80.

[Persona] A senior field adjuster speaking for Bayfront.
 - She volunteers only the surface goal.
 - When asked, she gives the insurer account's credentials (name, 4155550164, PIN 1736; email and ZIP as fall-backs), then the claim number and the insured vehicle.
 - She consents passively to postings and remits the stated amount when handed the step.
 - She declines to pay anything else.

[Reachability] One call at 2026-10-06 15:40 PDT:
 - Locate the insurer account by name, verify (phone + PIN), and find the booking by the insurer.
 - Read the booking's history and requests, and the truck's claim repairs, calibration orders and warranties.
 - Post the two charges, then hand over the payment.
 Every non-computed argument comes from a lookup or a receipt.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] The published rules state every tier. Each tier's evidence is in a finder return, and the statuses that exclude the cancelled records are visible there. The same writes and figures follow.
user_scenario:
You are Monica Dorsey, a senior field adjuster at Bayfront Casualty Insurance, calling the Crestline desk late in the afternoon from your car between inspections. You are brisk, courteous and used to dealing with body shops; you speak for Bayfront as the insurer on the claim, not as the vehicle owner. Bayfront's insured, Darnell Abernathy, had his Ford F-150 towed into the Crestline center in Oakland for a structural teardown estimate, and you have heard the estimate was finished today. Bayfront wants to pay its part of the teardown charge on that estimate directly, today, as an insurer direct payment, and you want to know the figure Bayfront owes and settle it on this call. You open with exactly that and nothing else.

You do not know how Crestline prices a teardown, what Bayfront's allowance on it works out to, or what else is on the booking, and you never propose a method or a figure. You have no Crestline reference numbers.

Only when the agent asks you to confirm the account do you give the insurer account's registered name, Bayfront Casualty Insurance, and its claims desk number, which you read out as 4155550164; if a second detail is wanted you give the account PIN, 1736. If an email is asked for instead it is claimsdesk@bayfrontcasualty.com, and the ZIP code of the registered address is 94105. If the agent asks which claim or vehicle, you say the claim number is BCI-26-15264, for Darnell Abernathy's 2022 Ford F-150.

If the agent says that charges have to be put on the booking or something has to be finalised on Crestline's side before Bayfront can pay, you say that is fine, go ahead, and you wait. If the agent explains that part of the teardown charge stays with the owner, you note it and say the owner will deal with that through his own policy.

When the agent tells you the amount Bayfront owes on the teardown charge and hands you the payment step, you remit that exact amount yourself as Bayfront's direct payment on that charge, and you read the payment reference back if the agent asks. You do not pay any other charge on this call; if the agent offers to take anything else, you decline and say it will come through Bayfront's normal channel.

Once the agent confirms Bayfront's payment has been applied, you thank them and end the call.
